messages.author: bea0a325f13d3b53
messages.subject: Effectplot {effects}
parts:
Dear all,
is there a possibility to display/png only a single panel of a plot created by: plot(allEffects(model), ... ,)) ?
I have an eight panel display (2 columns, 4 rows), style="stacked" and would like to create eight single plots for these different panels.
There is probably a very simple solution, but I cannot figure it out at the moment.
Best wishes,
Marco

I would send this to StatForLingWithR but here's a first thought
(hoping I don't misunderstand the question): don't plot

plot(allEffects(model))

but

plot(effect("variable.as.a.character.string", model))

Ok, I am not a member of the other group but I will try there later.
Thanks for the answer, but I am still not really able to do what I want to do.

I have a 4-level categorical response of a model with three interacting categorical predictors.
The predictors have 5, 4 and 2 levels respectively and I want to focus on the plots in which the 2-level predictor is set to "off".

In the allEffects plot I have a 2 column / 4 rows display with stacked bars for response. 
The left column shows the cases for the 2-level predictor="off". What I want to do is generate single plots for each of the four penals in the left hand column.

If I use plot(effect("variable.as.a.character.string", model)) I can focus on a single (non-interactive) effect, but I cannot focus on a panel for the interaction plot.

I hope this makes some sense....

Thanks again and best wishes, 
Marco

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Effectplot {effects}
parts: > If I use plot(effect("variable.as.a.character.string", model)) I can focus on a single (non-interactive) effect, but I cannot focus on a panel for the interaction plot.

You can also plot an interaction the same way but I myself do it as
described in the 2nd edition of the stats book: I generate a data
frame preds.hyp with everything I need from effect(), and then use
split/subset to access the parts I want.

Cheers,
